Chapter 10: Toward a New Kind of Care
When you look back on the journey of this family and their daughter, it’s clear their story isn’t just about tragedy or misunderstanding. It’s really a call to action—a reminder that our world is full of people who see things their own way. And when it comes to truly caring for someone, it takes more than just expertise.
It takes the courage to really listen... the humility to admit when we don’t have all the answers... and the willingness to reach out, even when it feels hard.
Across hospitals nationwide, the lessons from this family’s experience started to take root. Doctors and nurses began asking about what their patients believe, making space for rituals and traditions, and treating every encounter as a chance to truly connect.
Medical schools even started teaching students that maybe the most important question they can ask is simply, “What matters most to you?”
For the Hmong family, the road was anything but easy. They faced real loss, confusion, and heartbreak. But along the way, they also discovered moments of grace—little acts of kindness, unexpected moments of understanding, and that quiet strength that comes from holding onto hope, even when things feel impossible.
Their story stands as a testament to resilience, and a gentle reminder that healing can happen—even in the toughest times.
